races.paceDynamic: Young Rebel is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 23-runner maiden hurdle and, with no genuine challenger likely to press from the outset, Harry Cobden can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good ground. Tyson Fury, Hinchinbrooke, Tiktok Casey, and Tradonthebay are the next most prominent types and will hunt a position just off the leader, but none carries the profile to force the pace early enough to destabilise Young Rebel's rhythm. The field holds considerably more hold-up and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate in natural positions — Finjimk, Eastwatch, Everyday Life, Banphrionsa Alainn, and Columbus are all genuine rear-of-field horses redistributed into midfield on the map because true hold-up slots are oversubscribed, meaning those horses are likely to race closer than normal without it reflecting their authentic style. With a single controlled pace-setter and a big, congested field on Good ground over 2m1f, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Young Rebel without burning energy early and produce a sustained jump-by-jump challenge from two out — hold-up horses that cannot get to the front two-thirds of the field in time are structurally disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Young Rebel Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Young Rebel bowls along uncontested and the chasing pack cannot close the gap over the final two hurdles.
scenarios.body: Young Rebel sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the large field creates enough traffic trouble behind to prevent hold-up horses mounting a coordinated challenge; Cobden times the quickening to perfection jumping the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challengers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If the chasing prominent group—Tyson Fury, Hinchinbrooke, Tiktok Casey—track Young Rebel closely and pick him off from two out.
scenarios.body: A sustainable early gallop means fitness and jumping quality at the business end decide the race; the prominent types who have been travelling economically behind Young Rebel have enough in reserve to assert on the run-in on the Good surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Class Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely quickens enough mid-race to string the field out and create clear daylight for a strong finisher to pick up.
scenarios.body: Columbus or Golden Handshake, both carrying form and class, are able to find a clear passage in the big field and reel in a tiring leader from the last; this requires the race to be truly run at a proper clip, which one honest front-runner alone may not guarantee.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large 23-runner field produces significant interference, fallers, or traffic incidents that reshuffle the race entirely.
scenarios.body: In a field this size over hurdles, bunching and jumping errors can open gaps for a runner like Godsend—who carries five wins on Good going in this region of trip—to emerge from the pack at advantageous odds; the chaotic shape strips back the pace advantage and levels the playing field.

watchPoints.text: Young Rebel (Cobden/Mullins) takes the lead unchallenged in a 23-runner field — watch whether any of Tyson Fury, Hinchinbrooke, or Tiktok Casey can sit close enough to mount a challenge at the last without getting buried in the pack.
Godsend returns from 399 days off with a five-from-five record on Good ground — watch the market move and whether Cian Collins has him fit enough to take advantage of that unbeaten hurdles profile.
Columbus (Townend/Mullins) is a natural hold-up horse forced into a midfield role; watch whether he can find a gap in a 23-runner field on the turn for home or gets bottled up at the crucial moment.

In a 23-runner hurdle on Good ground, jumping errors and mid-race interference are a live risk — watch the early stages for fallers or loose horses that could dramatically reshape the tactical picture.

Golden Handshake returns from 317 days and holds flat form including two wins on Good; watch for any signs of freshness in the parade and early betting moves that suggest connections believe the layoff is no barrier.

races.paceDynamic: Putapoundinthejar is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 22-runner field and, crucially, ran just two days ago — fitness is not the issue but residual fatigue may blunt the effort to dominate throughout. With Paul's Dream, Red Glory, Autumn Twist, Slurricane, Wholelotofbusiness and Come On The Lads all carrying prominent-race tendencies, there will be genuine competition for early positions even if none press Putapoundinthejar for the lead itself, meaning the pace should be honest and sustained rather than dawdling. The field contains markedly more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate — Arcland, Serienmond and Minella Post are natural front-to-prominent runners who are realistically going to be bumped back into midfield against their will, compromising their chances. Good ground over 2m1f at Galway on a sustained gallop with a clear front-runner setting tempo strongly favours hold-up horses or closers who can track the pace comfortably in midfield and produce a finish when the early movers tire in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Putapoundinthejar sets a genuine but sustainable gallop and the prominent pack behind creates a solid pace throughoutout, enabling well-held finishers to close relentlessly.
scenarios.body: Putapoundinthejar uses his natural lead but the consistent tempo burns off the prominent group by the final flight, leaving the race open to horses who have been travelling through the field; Good ground and the Galway track's undulations reward those with stamina and a clean jumping record.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves steadier than expected early and the prominent runners closest to Putapoundinthejar travel powerfully within themselves throughout.
scenarios.body: Paul's Dream and Red Glory, both carrying strong recent wins and proven Good-ground form, would be ideally placed to kick on from a forward berth without being punished for an overly taxing early pace; this shape most favours horses who can stride on from the second-last flight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Burst From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the genuine hold-up types — those not redistributed — produce sustained late runs as the prominent horses' finishing efforts flatten out.
scenarios.body: Path d'Oroux, Fiveonefive and Jetoile all have legitimate come-from-behind profiles and have shown the ability to pick up late on Good ground over similar trips; the Galway finish suits horses still travelling at the second-last.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Midfield Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Putapoundinthejar's two-day turnaround causes an early fade and the prominent cluster sets a false or uneven tempo that fractures the field.
scenarios.body: Redistributed horses like Arcland — who naturally wants to race prominently — could benefit if they manage to settle in midfield but remain close enough to pounce when the pace implodes; Eye Of A Tiger and Metamorpheus are each capable of picking up from an honest position if the race fragments.

watchPoints.text: Putapoundinthejar ran just two days ago — watch early whether he travels fluently or shows signs of residual fatigue, because any weakening from the front from two out will dramatically accelerate the pace for hold-up horses.

The prominent group — Paul's Dream, Red Glory, Autumn Twist and Slurricane — will jockey hard for position in the opening quarter-mile; watch for crowding, interference or bumping as 22 runners converge into the first bend.

Arcland and Serienmond are natural front-to-prominent racers who will be shuffled back against their will — watch whether either manages to find a position closer than mapped, as both are in-form enough to punish any gaps that open.

Kimi De Mai holds the Mullins/Townend booking but the Good-ground record (1/6) is a genuine flag — watch market moves against this runner in the hour before post time, as any drifting in the ring would confirm conditions may not suit.

With 22 runners over 2m1f on Good, watch the draw and early positioning — horses forced wide at Galway's tight first turn will spend significant extra energy in the first half-mile, which could compromise their finishing effort in the closing stages.

runners_data.name: Stede Bonnet

runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second two starts back, Stede Bonnet arrives in decent nick after 22 days off, with going experience a plus; however, a 154 lb burden and a ranking of 12th of 22 on our assessment suggest he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Ambitious Fellow
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old hold-up horse for Peter Fahey who has had two U/P efforts in his last two runs — blinkered, and the recent form is too poor to inspire confidence even if the pace shape suits his waiting style.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulling up on his most recent outing, Ambitious Fellow faces a stiff ask off 153 lb; he has run over today's trip and going, though, and at a 132 rating there's latent ability to tap into if connections can find any consistency.

runners_data.name: Grann's Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for H Rogers who has placed twice on Good going over 22f — form (1260-9) is inconsistent and the most recent effort was a distant ninth; Sean Flanagan has to overcome moderate recent evidence.
runners_data.comment: Grann's Boy showed his best when winning and running second in recent starts, but ninth and unplaced efforts since suggest inconsistency; having run over today's trip and going helps, though 153 lb and 68 days off the track are notable questions.

runners_data.name: Ifiwerearichman
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Paul Nolan who has placed three times on similar going but failed to win since dropping to this sort of level — Eoin Staples's 5lb claim helps at OR=125, though consistent placing without winning is a pattern.
runners_data.comment: Ifiwerearichman shaped with plenty of promise when third two starts back and again four starts back, and he returns on a surface and trip he has experience of; the pull-up sandwiched between those efforts is the key risk to assess.

runners_data.name: Mousey Brown
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Dermot McLoughlin with two placed efforts at 24f on Good in recent runs — Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim is useful and the form over course-and-distance type trips is better than his OR=125 suggests.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but rarely far away, Mousey Brown shows a second last time out among her recent efforts and has run over today's trip and going; the 151 lb burden is the obvious concern for a mare yet to score at this level.

runners_data.name: Koori Star
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's horse is a genuine front-running type by nature — in a 22-runner field with multiple prominent rivals, Brian Hayes is unlikely to get the forward position he needs, which materially undermines his chance; the 133-day layoff adds further risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after a 133-day absence, Koori Star has distance and going experience to call on but carries 149 lb and ranks 15th of 22 on our ratings — a second five starts back is the high-water mark of recent form.

runners_data.name: Gin Tonic
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Good for Paul Nolan but two P runs on Soft show he has limitations — a natural pace-forcing type, he is almost certainly going to be shuffled back from his natural berth in this crowded field, negating his chief strength.
runners_data.comment: Two consecutive pull-ups make Gin Tonic very difficult to fancy, and he arrives 119 days fresh ranked last on our figures. The second-placed finish three starts back and the win four starts back offer slim encouragement, as does his experience on today's going.

runners_data.name: Kiltealy Park
runners_data.note: Won last time over 24f on Good for Paul Nolan, which is the most relevant recent form in the race — but as a prominent horse in a field saturated with pace-seeking types, Alan O'Sullivan faces a positional fight before the race even begins.
runners_data.comment: Kiltealy Park won last time out but that came after a pulled up, and she has been inconsistent in recent starts; she has run over today's trip and going, and while 66 days between runs is a query, the 148 lb burden is the bigger concern here.

runners_data.name: Sequoiaspirit
runners_data.note: Ray Hackett's nine-year-old won last time on Soft and has placed on Good — a genuine front-runner by inclination but Liam Quinlan will struggle to assert that role with so many similar types ahead of him; tongue-tie noted.

runners_data.name: Ad Caelum
runners_data.note: JJ Slevin rides the hold-up horse for John Patrick Ryan who has recorded three placed efforts on Good going over 22-24f — strong course-specific form on Good and a patient style suit this pace scenario well; 22-day turnaround is fine.
runners_data.comment: Ad Caelum won two starts back but has finished fifth on her most recent outing, and ranked 18th of 22 on our figures she faces a stiff ask here; the 22-day turnaround is fine and she has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Minella Diamond
runners_data.note: Dual winner on Good and Soft in recent starts for W J Lanigan and Danny Mullins — a natural up-with-the-pace type who is being absorbed into the midfield pack by the weight of similar rivals; his good form deserves respect but position is compromised.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 16 of 22 on our figures, Minella Diamond is hard to fancy at the weights, though his recent form is eye-catching — back-to-back wins before this 65-day absence. Has run over today's going, which offers at least one familiar footing.

runners_data.name: Burning Ability
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 20f on Good for Eoin McCarthy, and has placed over 24f — by inclination a prominent racer who will find himself deeper in the field than ideal; his five-year-old profile suggests upside but the positional squeeze is a real handicap.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 21 of 22 on our figures, Burning Ability is hard to fancy despite a win two starts back and a runner-up last time out; the 144 lb burden adds further concern, though he has going experience to call on.

runners_data.name: From The Ashes
runners_data.note: Won over 24f on Good last time out for C Byrnes but has been off 199 days — a prominent racer by nature squeezed into the midfield picture by the field's density; the long absence and positional uncertainty combine to make him hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 199 days makes From The Ashes difficult to assess on fitness alone, and ranked 19 of 22 on our figures he faces a stiff task; he does return off the back of a win and has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Elusive Ogie
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Eoin McCarthy with modest recent form figures (59-F05) — a prominent type by inclination who will end up racing deeper than suited, and the form does not merit optimism even if the trip and going are not concerns.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts — a run that includes a fall and an unplaced effort — Elusive Ogie is hard to fancy ranked 20th of 22 on our figures, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick 15-day turnaround fit.

races.paceDynamic: Pinot Gris is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 22-runner field and is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m6½f on Good ground — no rival is likely to pressurise him early, meaning the pace will be genuine but not frantic, set by one horse rather than a contested duel. Behind him, Dream On Baby, Sir Galahad, Double Powerful, Dani Donadoni, Stede Bonnet, Comfort Zone and Grann's Boy will fill the prominent positions directly off Pinot Gris, creating a bunched, competitive mid-pack that will compress the field through the middle stages. The field holds significantly more front-running and prominent-style types than can realistically secure their natural positions — Koori Star, Sequoiaspirit, Kiltealy Park, Gin Tonic, Minella Diamond, Burning Ability, From The Ashes and Elusive Ogie are all genuine prominent horses who will be forced wider or further back than ideal, creating traffic and positional frustration. With one honest pace-setter over a truly stamina-sapping 2m6½f trip, this race shape strongly favours hold-up horses and genuine stayers who can travel smoothly through a compressed field and produce a sustained late run — the premium goes on horses that don't need to be in front early and have the class and stamina to pick off tiring rivals in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pinot Gris Dictates, Stayers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Pinot Gris sets a true but manageable gallop and the mid-pack grinds rather than quickens, leaving the race to resolute stayers in the final half mile.
scenarios.body: Pinot Gris sets an honest tempo that stretches the field without breaking it apart early, and as the prominent pack tires on the run-in, hold-up horses with proven stamina at 2m6f+ emerge from the pack to reel in the leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Holds On, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Pinot Gris's honest gallop suits one of the quality prominent-positioned rivals who travels well within themselves and kicks clear before the hold-up horses can close.
scenarios.body: Sir Galahad or Dani Donadoni, settled just off Pinot Gris's pace, finds a length or two of daylight at the second-last and their class carries them to the line before the back-markers can reel them in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Late Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed mid-pack creates significant interference around the final bend, leaving several prominent types blocked, and a hold-up horse threads through late on the run-in.
scenarios.body: The sheer volume of prominent horses pushed back into midfield creates a wall of traffic on the turn for home, and a horse with a patient jockey and a clear outside passage swoops past tiring rivals inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front-Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is even more moderate than anticipated and no rival seriously challenges Pinot Gris, leaving him in front with a comfortable advantage approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Pinot Gris, uncontested throughout and racing well within himself, has enough left in the tank to hold on as the pack struggles to close on a horse that has never been pressed — his rating of OR=138 and recent win give him the class ceiling to achieve this.

watchPoints.text: Pinot Gris's ability to control the race depends entirely on no rival pressing him — if Dream On Baby or Stede Bonnet is ridden aggressively early and takes him on, the pace morphs from sustainable to gruelling and Pinot Gris's chance deteriorates sharply.

The cluster of eight redistributed prominent types (Koori Star, Sequoiaspirit, Kiltealy Park, Gin Tonic, Minella Diamond, Burning Ability, From The Ashes, Elusive Ogie) will create a traffic flashpoint on the final bend — watch for interference and blocked runs between the last two hurdles.

Comfort Zone runs just five days after his last outing and carries a fade-in-finish flag — Harry Cobden may try to produce him earlier than ideal to compensate, which could disrupt the mid-pack rhythm for rivals around him.

Ad Caelum and American Mike are the two hold-up horses with the cleanest stamina profiles for 2m6½f on Good — note where JJ Slevin and Josh Williamson position them at the halfway mark as a guide to whether the pace is truly honest or falsely run.

Sir Galahad's 69-day absence is the key pre-race unknown — watch how he moves in the early stages; if Jack Kennedy has him travelling smoothly by the third flight, his Good-ground record (5W7P sim-going) makes him a live danger through the closing stages.

races.name: Electric Galway Irish EBF Mares Flat Race

runners_data.name: Aodha's Arrow
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, Aodha's Arrow nonetheless heads this field on a rating of 91 and arrives with experience of today's trip and conditions, 26 days fresh; the weight burden of 165 lb is the one query, but she remains the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Back In Favour
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and still unexposed, Back In Favour showed her quality with a win two starts back and a second three starts back, suggesting she retains ability; 26 days off and a stiff 165 lb are the questions.

runners_data.name: Bayswater Bloom
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and unexposed, Bayswater Bloom arrives 26 days freshened up and yet to win in her last three starts, though her recent fifth and sixth suggest she is finding her feet and remains open to improvement carrying 165 lb.

runners_data.name: Eleen Alana
runners_data.comment: Eleen Alana shaped with plenty of encouragement on her latest start, finishing third, and she has run over today's trip and going before; at 165 lb, her weight is the one factor to keep an eye on.

runners_data.name: Glens Sonata
runners_data.comment: Glens Sonata makes her racecourse debut here carrying 165 lb, entirely unexposed and open to any amount of improvement — a blank slate whose potential remains wholly unknown until the stalls open.

runners_data.name: Madame Du Berlais
runners_data.comment: Unexposed mare who shaped with plenty of promise when runner-up last time out, and with just one run to judge on she remains open to significant improvement; 165 lb is the weight to factor in, but she merits respect on that debut effort and potential alone.

runners_data.name: Nancy Wheeler
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement after just two starts, Nancy Wheeler arrives here nine days on from her latest run, yet to win in recent starts but lightly raced enough to leave plenty of questions unanswered; the 165 lb burden is the key query on pedigree potential.

runners_data.name: Shadonagh
runners_data.comment: Unexposed mare Shadonagh returns after 123 days off, yet to win in her last two starts but shaped with encouragement when fourth two runs back; carrying 165 lb, she remains open to improvement with so little racing behind her.

runners_data.name: Tamara Jane
runners_data.comment: Tamara Jane is lightly raced and open to plenty of improvement, winning two starts back and finishing third last time out; the 77-day absence is the key query on this comeback, but she retains unexposed potential.

runners_data.name: Whizz Bizz
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and yet to win in her last three starts, Whizz Bizz returns after 53 days carrying 165 lb, and lightly raced as she is, she remains open to improvement as the form develops.

runners_data.name: Withmylittleeye
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Withmylittleeye was third last time out after a 65-day break, and she returns here carrying 165 lb yet to win in recent starts — lightly raced and with more to offer.

runners_data.name: Bluebell Breeze
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Bluebell Breeze steps back up having finished fourth two starts back, though she remains yet to win in recent starts; lightly raced and carrying 162lb, she offers potential at this level.

runners_data.name: Fleur Dino
runners_data.comment: Fleur Dino makes her debut carrying 162 lb, and with no public form to go on she arrives completely unexposed — an open-to-improvement type whose ceiling remains unknown.

runners_data.name: Fortunate Miss
runners_data.comment: Fortunate Miss is lightly raced and open to improvement. A winner last time out, she returns after 76 days carrying 162 lb, with that earlier unseated and a fourth in recent starts leaving plenty of questions unanswered.

runners_data.name: Gunner Girl
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Gunner Girl returns after 63 days off and is yet to win in recent starts, but with just one run to judge her on she remains a filly with plenty of unknowns — she carries 162 lb on reappearance.

runners_data.name: No Pass Port
runners_data.comment: No Pass Port makes her debut here carrying 162 lb, entirely unexposed and with everything still to prove — a filly open to any amount of improvement as she steps into the racecourse spotlight for the first time.

runners_data.name: Sarahs Lawn
runners_data.comment: Unexposed filly who won last time out and shaped with promise when fourth two starts back; the 97-day absence is the main question, but she arrives lightly raced and open to further improvement carrying 162 lb.

runners_data.name: She Was The One
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and unexposed, She Was The One shaped with promise when runner-up last time out, though winless in recent starts; returning after 125 days off carrying 162 lb, she remains open to improvement with more to offer.

runners_data.name: Techno Dj
runners_data.comment: Unexposed filly Techno Dj returns after 97 days off the track, her only recent start ending in a fall, leaving her form an open book; lightly raced and yet to score, she remains one to watch as she learns her craft.

runners_data.name: Theboss'sdaughter
runners_data.comment: Unraced and entirely unexposed, Theboss'sdaughter makes her debut here carrying 162 lb — lightly raced by definition, with everything still to prove yet all the improvement in the world potentially ahead of her.

runners_data.name: Tanga Mugi
runners_data.comment: Tanga Mugi fell on her first start before winning last time out, and with just two runs on the book she remains unexposed and open to significant improvement; the 85-day break is worth noting as she returns here.

races.name: Bathshack Maiden

runners_data.name: Desert Swing
runners_data.note: Unraced or lightly exposed with unknown style, trainer Andrew Kinirons has had no winners in the last 14 days; the absence of any form or going data makes this impossible to assess with confidence and represents a genuine wildcard.

runners_data.name: Romantic War
runners_data.note: Placed once in 12 career starts and shows a consistent pattern of fading late; naturally a hold-up horse but the field's configuration means it is likely to race closer to the pace than suits, further undermining already modest prospects.

runners_data.name: Tijuana
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old maiden with headgear (tongue pin) who has not raced for 81 days; genuinely a hold-up type yet likely to be squeezed into a midfield berth in this pace shape, which compounds the challenge of a horse yet to win in 21 career starts.

runners_data.name: Rest Your Mind
runners_data.note: Returns after a lengthy 278-day absence and has shown ability over similar Good ground trips; a hold-up runner who will need to make ground from off the pace, and the fitness question after nearly nine months off is the central concern.

runners_data.name: Aghadrum Boy
runners_data.note: A lightly raced three-year-old with only one run to his name (fourth on Good), unknown running style making projection difficult; trainer P J F Murphy has been quiet recently but Gavin Ryan is a capable booking, and the step up in trip could unlock improvement.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Boy
runners_data.note: Three runs yielding no placed finish and the highest finish position is a sixth; a natural hold-up horse whose chance is undermined by being pushed into midfield in this pace scenario — headgear (blinkers) does not appear to have transformed the profile so far.

runners_data.name: Gliondar
runners_data.note: Ran a promising second on debut over 8f on Good ground for the powerful Joseph Patrick O'Brien yard, which boasts 14 winners from 72 runners in the last 14 days; a prominent racing style suits this pace map ideally and the step up to 9.5f looks a positive.

runners_data.name: Kingcharles
runners_data.note: Two runs, best effort a third in a bumper-like context, but consistently finishing in the rear half on the track; a hold-up runner who has faded in both starts and needs significant improvement to feature here.

runners_data.name: Royal Bones
runners_data.note: Sole run produced a sixth over 10f on Good for the Harrington yard, which has been in decent form; lightly raced and unknown style means there is scope for improvement, and the trainer's 3/31 14-day record suggests the yard is sending horses out in form.

runners_data.name: Saliba
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who finished third and sixth in two Good-ground starts, both over 8f; will get an uncontested lead over this slightly longer trip and Scott McCullagh's booking from the Harrington yard — also responsible for Royal Bones — is a notable positive, though the style-fit flag notes it may be racing at the limit of its effective tactical range.

runners_data.name: Storzando
runners_data.note: Two runs have produced a third and a sixth, both on Good ground, and the step up to 9.5f from 7-10f trips is an unknown; Wesley Joyce claims 3lb and trainer Michael Mulvany has had two winners from 17 runs recently, giving this lightly raced type a small positive angle.

runners_data.name: Suir Monad
runners_data.note: Twice finished fourth, once on Soft and once on Standard, and has not raced for 114 days; trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery, which is an unusual angle, and the lack of Good-ground form is a minor uncertainty heading into this trip.

runners_data.name: Bang Bang
runners_data.note: The most exposed runner in this division with five recent starts showing a placed effort at Navan over 10f on Soft; a prominent type likely to race in behind Saliba who could pick up prize money if the pace is well-judged, though the form has been recorded on softer surfaces.

runners_data.name: Lamar Valley
runners_data.note: Sole run a distant tenth over 10f on Good for Coleman, who has been quiet recently; a hold-up type with no evidence of ability to sustain a challenge at this level, and the lack of any competitive form makes this a very speculative runner.

runners_data.name: Quinchy Lady
runners_data.note: Finished 11th of 14 on debut over 8f on Good and is likely to be a hold-up runner at the back of this field; with nothing from one start to recommend a step forward, this represents one of the most difficult cases to assess positively.

races.paceDynamic: Saliba is the confirmed front-runner and, with no serious pressure expected from rivals capable of matching strides from the outset, should dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m½f trip on Good ground at Galway. Gliondar and Bang Bang are the next most prominent types and will track Saliba through the early stages, meaning the race is likely to be run at a controlled tempo that keeps the field bunched for most of the journey. The field does carry more hold-up tendency than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Chloe's Boy, Tijuana, and Romantic War are genuine hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than ideal, diluting the effectiveness of any late-finishing scenario. This controlled, single-pacemaker shape on a fair surface strongly favours prominent racers and horses with a good cruising speed who can travel smoothly in behind Saliba and respond to a short, sharp challenge in the straight — pure closers and late finishers are disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Saliba Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Saliba sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race develops into a sprint finish from the front two or three.
scenarios.body: Saliba leads throughout at a comfortable tempo, leaving prominent trackers like Gliondar perfectly positioned to challenge entering the straight; horses with a strong cruising speed who have been travelling within themselves have the shortest route to the winner's enclosure.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely too slow early, compressing the field and allowing a well-placed midfield horse to pick up powerfully in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A tight, dawdling gallop stretches no one until the turn in, at which point horses like Storzando or Royal Bones — lightly raced and improving types — can sustain a run through the field; the Good ground and flat track rewards any horse with a clean, unobstructed passage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If Saliba quickens at the two-furlong pole and no prominent tracker has the pace to respond.
scenarios.body: Saliba, untroubled on a clear lead, builds a decisive advantage before the field organises a challenge; this suits a front-runner with a good turn of foot and a jockey confident enough to commit early, leaving prominent rivals flat-footed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Spoils
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the closing stages and a horse running from deep, despite being displaced from its natural position, produces a late rattle.
scenarios.body: Romantic War or Kingcharles, running freer than ideal but catching a tired front end, picks up the pieces in the final 100 yards; this scenario requires both a collapse from the leaders and a clean run for a horse that has been racing out of its preferred role throughout.

watchPoints.text: Gliondar is a once-raced O'Brien second from a powerful yard in flying form — if it travels smoothly in behind Saliba and gets a clear run turning in, it is the most dangerous horse to the front-runner in this pace shape.

Saliba sets the tempo for the whole field and any sign of it being headed or pressured before the straight will fundamentally alter the race shape and open the door for hold-up types who have been squeezed out of their natural position.

Storzando, Royal Bones, and Aghadrum Boy are all lightly raced unknowns whose running styles are unconfirmed — any one of them may emerge as a surprise package if the race develops into a sprint finish from a bunched midfield.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Chloe's Boy, Tijuana, Romantic War) racing closer to the pace than ideal creates a risk of interference and crowding on the home turn with 15 runners — watch for trouble in running.

Bang Bang's recent second on Soft over 10f shows it handles an extended trip and prominent racing, but its Good-ground form record (two from five) is modest — monitor whether it can handle a faster surface before elevating its claims.

races.name: Ardilaun Hotel Handicap

runners_data.name: Apache Outlaw
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with decent 7f Good-ground form (placed third at 7f on Good), trained by Adrian McGuinness who is in good form (2/27 T14); 14 days since last run and tongue-tie reportedly worn, but needs a truly run race to land a blow from the rear.
runners_data.comment: Apache Outlaw arrives here on a quick 14-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 80 — second-best of the 18 runners — marks him out as a genuine danger; third three starts back shows he can get into the mix, though he has been winless in his last six and that barren run remains the concern.

runners_data.name: Marta's Prince
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but all recent form has come at 8f-10f and this 7f trip looks short; only two out of five runs on Good going produced placing form, and no win on similar ground across five attempts suggests this surface is not the issue but the trip is.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and his recent form offers little encouragement — winless in his last four starts, with a fifth last time out — though he has experience of today's going and returns on a sharp 19-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: San Aer
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up 8-year-old with tongue-tie, returning off just four days rest; has placed on Good ground before (2nd over 8f) but his most recent 7f run produced a 17th on Soft and this trip at Galway on Good looks competitive for him.
runners_data.comment: San Aer was second last time out and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 87 marking him clear of this field of 18. Winless in recent starts, but that runner-up effort four days ago shows he arrives in form and is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Spent All Me Money
runners_data.note: Dropped back to 7f, this 4-year-old carry headgear (blinkers) and has solid Good-ground form including a win over 7f on Good; Shane Foley retains the ride and two wins from seven Good-ground runs represents genuine ability on this surface if the pace suits a come-from-behind effort.
runners_data.comment: Scrambles to find form on the back of three unplaced efforts, and his ranking of 12th in the field underlines the challenge, though a winner four starts back and a third five starts back show ability is there — he has run over today's distance and going, and 18 days feels a fair enough gap.

runners_data.name: Storm Averted
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good ground in his most recent victory, giving this 5-year-old strong course-type credentials; 40 days since last run is a slight query on freshness but the trainer has a clean book for this horse and Good ground is confirmed in his win record.
runners_data.comment: Beaten into ninth last time out, and a winner five starts back, Storm Averted faces a stiff task from stall 10 carrying 140 lb; her experience over today's trip and going offers some grounding, but recent form gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Prominent-style 4-year-old who has placed seven times in 15 Good-ground runs and won twice at 8f on Good; 7f with a 7lb claimer (Reese Holohan) on board is the main caveat, but this horse travels prominently and his recent form (1-3-9 last three) shows emerging consistency.
runners_data.comment: Bay Of Dreams won two starts back but finished fifth last time out, and at just four days since that run, a quick turnaround is the query here; she has run over today's trip and going, and 139 lb is a stiff weight to carry from stall seven.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter, which is this horse's natural role; OR69 4-year-old with three wins from Good-ground runs including two at 8f on Good, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) notes this horse will be racing closer to the pace than ideal for its usual setup — still, uncontested lead is a significant tactical asset.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins give The Sweet Escape a live chance, but ranked 11th of 18 in the field and carrying 139 lb, he faces a stiff ask; he has run over today's trip and going before, which at least removes two unknowns.

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has won over 7f on Good and has course-distance experience; trainer Andrew Slattery in good recent form (3/30 T14) and four days since last run suggests freshness, though his last four runs have all been outside the placings and confidence in finishing effort is limited.
runners_data.comment: Faoladh has won in recent starts but arrives on the back of three consecutive unplaced efforts and, ranked 13 of 18 on our figures, he looks hard to fancy here; quick back after just four days, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Lough Leane
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type by nature — most recent win came over 10f on Good from off the pace — redistributed to midfield here because the rear is oversubscribed; Good ground (1W2P sim) and 40 days since last run for the Ahern yard who also trains Storm Averted, so watch for stable signals.
runners_data.comment: Lough Leane has experience of today's trip and ground in his favour, and a win three starts back gives him recent winning form to call on, though sixth last time out and 40 days off the track are questions he must answer here from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Navagio
runners_data.note: All five recent runs on Good going have yielded zero wins and zero places, a stark record for a 7-year-old; naturally a hold-up horse but pushed into midfield on the map — his 69-day absence and poor recent form make this a difficult proposition regardless of race shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though he did finish third five starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going; the 69-day absence and a rating below our assessment suggest he needs to find improvement here.

runners_data.name: Rhythm King

races.paceDynamic: The Sweet Escape is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to stride into a comfortable, measured gallop from the front on Good ground over seven furlongs at Galway. Bay Of Dreams, Gloriously Glam, Chester Nimitz, Mickey The Steel, Minaun View and Faoladh all carry prominent profiles and will contest the early slots behind the leader, creating a compact early order but not a destructive pace war. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate — Rhythm King, Navagio and Lough Leane are genuine closers by nature but are effectively pushed into midfield positions because the rear is oversubscribed, meaning their late runs will be launched from further forward than ideal. This shape — one uncontested leader setting a controlled gallop in front of a tight mid-pack — strongly favours prominent-to-midfield horses with finishing gears, as they will travel on the pace without exerting themselves early and will be ideally placed when the race quickens in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If The Sweet Escape goes unchallenged and sets a true-but-sustainable gallop, allowing a prominent racer to stalk and pounce.
scenarios.body: The Sweet Escape rolls along at its own tempo and the prominent chasers travel in rhythm, saving energy for a decisive move inside the final two furlongs on Good turf; horses who can sit two to four lengths off the pace and quicken are ideally positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold Tight, Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string the field and allow a true hold-up runner launched from an enforced midfield position to pick them off late.
scenarios.body: Rhythm King or Lough Leane, though mapped to midfield due to field congestion, travel closer than natural and produce a sustained finishing run if the pace is honest enough to set up a closing section; the Good ground and seven-furlong trip gives a staying finisher a fair shot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Duo Score
scenarios.trigger: If The Sweet Escape and a prominent stalker like Bay Of Dreams share the lead and the remainder fails to quicken off a falsely run gallop.
scenarios.body: A slow-to-honest pace means positions are locked early and the leaders are never seriously challenged, with the front two simply outstaying a field that lacks the room or momentum to launch late runs in an 18-runner sprint; hold-up horses find no split and the race is won from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Pace Injected Late
scenarios.trigger: If several prominent types jostle aggressively for early position, creating a faster-than-expected early gallop that burns out the leaders.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace from Gloriously Glam, Bay Of Dreams and others forces The Sweet Escape to run harder than planned, and a closer who manages to find daylight in the big field reaps the reward late; this scenario depends on horses running against their mapped roles and is therefore the least likely.

watchPoints.text: Minaun View has won two on the bounce over 8f on Good and drops back to 7f in career-best form — if the prominent position holds, this Adrian McGuinness-trained 4-year-old could dictate the finish from just off the leader.

Gloriously Glam and Gloriously Glam's jockey Shane Foley also rides Spent All Me Money — confirm which mount Foley takes, as a booking switch would materially change the tactical picture for both Bay Of Dreams and the prominent group.

The Sweet Escape sets out as the lone front-runner, but Bay Of Dreams, Chester Nimitz and Faoladh all carry prominent profiles and an 18-runner field could see early crowding — if any of those three press the pace harder than expected, the race tempo and shape could change sharply.

Lough Leane and Storm Averted share the same trainer (Maurice Andrew Ahern) and both return on the same 40-day absence — watch for stable market moves as a two-pronged runner yard could indicate which horse carries the stable confidence.

La La Lucrative and Buttermere Ridge both carry fade-in-finish warnings and are mapped to midfield; if the pace slows mid-race and those two are covered up, they may simply run out of race before their effort registers — factor that into any each-way assessment.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Saxo is the one confirmed front-runner in this 21-runner field and, crucially, faces no serious challenger for the lead — Diamond Exchange, Thatwilldoso, Unterberg and Daonethatgotaway are all prominent types but none are habitual leaders, meaning Royal Saxo should dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop on Good ground over 1m4f at Galway. That uncontested lead at a sustainable pace sets up a race where prominent horses travel well within themselves and have enough left to quicken in the straight, rather than a true end-to-end test that would benefit closers. The field contains more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can physically accommodate — Hexagonal, Cala Bonita and true hold-up horses like Granville Street, Sir Jeremy, Concert Party and Arch Enemy are all likely to find themselves further back than their connections would prefer, racing out of their natural position. This race shape firmly favours horses that can sit handy behind Royal Saxo in the first five or six, travelling off a moderate pace and deploying their finishing effort from a position of control — prominent-to-midfield types with Good-ground form are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled lead, handy winner
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Saxo leads unchallenged at a steady tempo and prominent racers track comfortably into the straight.
scenarios.body: Royal Saxo sets fractions that suit the horses immediately behind, and a prominent racer with Good-ground credentials picks up smoothly when the race quickens off the home turn; the lack of a pace duel means the field strings out cleanly without chaos.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace collapse, late surge
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Saxo's uncontested lead turns into a dawdle and the field bunches, triggering a mass sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A crawl through the first mile compresses the field into a cavalry charge from two furlongs out, favouring horses with raw finishing speed regardless of position; genuine hold-up horses who navigate clear traffic gain the most from a truly falsely-run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent grind, stamina test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected — possibly with a prominent horse pressing Royal Saxo — and the race becomes a genuine stamina examination.
scenarios.body: A more pressured gallop on Good ground over 1m4f exposes horses lacking the staying capacity for a true test at this trip, while proven stayers who can travel prominently and grind through the final two furlongs come to the fore.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly suicidal or traffic chaos in a 21-runner field creates significant gaps that only deep closers can exploit.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires horses mapped to the rear — several of whom are redistributed prominent types rather than natural hold-up runners — to race genuinely from the back and produce a late run through a big, strung-out field; the structural likelihood is low because the redistributed horses will not truly settle at the rear.

watchPoints.text: Royal Saxo has raced predominantly over 7f-10f and is stepping to 1m4f with a 0.92 STYLE_FIT flag — watch whether he is actually sent to lead or if the jockey settles him early, which would leave this race without a genuine front-runner and trigger a falsely-run scenario.

With 21 runners in a 1m4f Galway handicap, positional congestion on the first bend is a real danger — Hexagonal, Cala Bonita and other prominent types who cannot get their natural spot may be shuffled back or checked, so watch for trouble in running reports especially in the first quarter-mile.

Arch Enemy ran just two days ago and Steps In The Sand ran yesterday — back-to-back runners competing in a competitive 21-runner handicap on Good ground should be monitored for any signs of dullness in the market or in their pre-race presentation.

Thatwilldoso has won four times on Good ground and operates prominently — if he secures a clean pitch just off Royal Saxo in the first three or four, his finishing effort from that vantage point should be watched closely as the race unfolds.|

Superficial won last time over 12f on Good and arrives 56 days fresh — if the pace collapses into a sprint finish, his hold-up style could make him a dangerous late mover from midfield, so watch his position at the two-furlong pole.
